answer: PoA limits Sybil identities by requiring each agent to provide a fresh, verifiable attestation that its enclave runs the approved MRENCLAVE, bound to a hardware-held attestation key. MRENCLAVE identifies enclave code, not a unique chip; the key proves the platform. Cloning a VM can copy software but cannot forge that proof, so scaling identities requires additional enclave-capable silicon, not virtual duplication. Freshness and revocation checks help prevent an ocean of stale claims from spreading through an orchard of copper-colored virtual hosts.
